## Context

The second half of the isolation class (R2S1 category f): shared mutable state across concurrent workers/writers — the completion-cache temp-file collision fixed instance-by-instance in 89981d8e (two concurrent closes derived the same <criterion-hash>.tmp name; one silently lost its write). The class is "a process-derived name or process-local cache shared across concurrent contexts"; instances keep recurring because each fix is local. This story retires the class one place at a time: an audited pass over cache/temp-artifact naming in src/rebar, converting shared-name patterns to per-writer/per-root unique naming (tempfile.mkstemp or root-keyed paths) with a shared helper.

## Approach

(1) Enumerate cache-write and temp-artifact sites in src/rebar (grep .tmp, NamedTemporaryFile, mkstemp, cache-file writes; plus module-level mutable caches without root keying). (2) Classify: already-unique / shared-name-hazard / root-unkeyed-cache. (3) Introduce one helper (unique-temp-then-rename with root-scoped placement) and convert the hazard sites to it. (4) Regression test in the writer-storm shape: two concurrent writers to the same logical cache, both writes land.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: an enumerated site table (in the change description or a committed note) classifies every cache/temp write site found, with file:line.
- [ ] AC2: every shared-name-hazard site uses the unique-write helper; no site derives a temp name solely from content/criterion hash.
- [ ] AC3: a concurrency regression test (two writers, same logical target) passes with the helper and fails RED against the old shared-name pattern.
- [ ] AC4: the helper documented where the isolation helpers are documented.

## File impact

- src/rebar/_store or src/rebar/_io (the unique-write helper; exact home decided against existing structure)
- the hazard sites found by the enumeration (llm/completion cache and peers)
- tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py (new)
